title: George Lasry’s decipherment of a Latin diplomatic letter (DECODE R4282, Chifferklaver låda II:113)

documents.shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Stockholm, Chifferklaver låda II:113; DECODE R4282
documents.date: Undated; DECODE catalogue range 1600–1699 is not an independently established date
documents.route: Unknown sender and recipient; report concerns England

plaintext.source: No separate or interlinear decipherment used. Four original cleartext passages occur within the letter.

transcription.source: George Lasry using CTTS (CrypTool Transcriber and Solver), from DECODE R4282 manuscript images; symbol classifications refined with GPT-6 Astra.
transcription.notes: 25 lines on page 1 and 7 on page 2. Counts exclude 104 separator marks and 11 punctuation marks. Positions and icons preserve CTTS identifiers; no other document is counted.

system.summary: A Latin graphical homophonic substitution with vowel homophones, a QU sign, eleven null signs and three unresolved apparent word signs.

diacritics.note: Distinct graphical signs are preserved by their CTTS classes; no separate modifier rule is claimed.

system.doubled_letters: Usually written twice; the readable edition retains explicit orthographic normalization.
system.notes: The three apparent word signs are distinct and unidentified. The CTTS solver name describes the recovery tool, not an unsupported claim about word-sign values.

prior_solution.where: No earlier decipherment was used. The 2026-09-21 repository survey records a failed attempt. DECODE was marked Non-decrypted on 2026-10-14; this is not proof that no prior reading exists.

conditions.human_role: Solved by George Lasry, who transcribed the cipher in CTTS, used its built-in homophonic solver for initial key recovery, directed refinement, corrected sign readings and supplied the result for contribution. GPT-6 Astra assisted in improving and finalizing the key and decryption.

solution.what: George Lasry transcribed the two manuscript pages with CTTS, preserving graphic sign classes, separators and page/line positions. The solver origin is also recorded in key.txt. Exact initial session date is not reconstructed.

George Lasry recovered the initial key using the CTTS built-in homophonic solver, as expressly confirmed by him. No run log survives in this package, so restart counts, scores, timing and implementation details are not invented.

GPT-6 Astra assisted Lasry with Latin analysis and image checks to improve and finalize the key and reading: (31) changed from O to D, several apparent letters became nulls, and (37)/(38)/(39) remained separate unknown word signs rather than L/P/C. These are superseded assignments, not documented failed solver runs.
Compared both pages and the four original cleartext spans; integrated them in manuscript order, preserving five editorial restorations separately from literal cipher output.

Checked the live DECODE record and its three attachments: wrapper plus two displayed text-page views. Recorded Riksarkivet shelfmark and catalogue range without assigning an exact date or correspondents.

Reapplied the current CTTS key to every transcribed sign and reproduced the literal decryption. Counted 1084 signs: 800 mapped non-null, 279 nulls, 5 occurrences of 3 unresolved signs. Excluded 27 token positions within five editorially restored words from the conservative coherence floor.

Read the existing riksarkivet1628 repository notes: the 21 September attempt reported no Latin from earlier transcription/annealing. No prior decipherment found in the inspected materials; an exhaustive publication search is not claimed.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1079 tokens, 36 types, la order 4: reading -2.17 per letter; random keys -4.847 (z 9.5); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.479 (mean -3.506, z 87.6); annealer on the real text -2.17. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.17; polyphony 0.0; 5 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.17

outcome.method_basis: Primary achievement: George Lasry recovered the key with CTTS’s built-in homophonic solver from the ciphertext; GPT-6 Astra helped refine the key and reading, with original cleartext context incorporated later and no historical decipherment or external key used.
outcome.fraction_read_source: token_readings.tsv: 800 mapped of 805 non-null cipher occurrences; 279 nulls counted separately. Full key assignment is 1079/1084. This measures assignments, not independently verified accuracy.

credits.note: Solved by George Lasry: CTTS transcription and built-in homophonic solver; key and decryption improved and finalized with GPT-6 Astra.

gaps.detail: Names or titles remain unidentified; no identity is supplied from speculation.
SIMPIR, AGLO, PRSRSVS, PRSMITAT and IT are retained in literal output; readable Latin marks contextual restoration, not proven new mappings.

outcome.notes: Both text pages covered in full. The conservative coherence floor 773/805 excludes all 27 tokens in five restored words plus 5 open word tokens. This is not an LLM-only break or a first-publication claim.
